name: gallery
title: Gallery
rationale: Gallery treats the menu like a well-lit shop window: a warm off-white canvas, large product photography and quiet chrome, so the products do the selling. Purple is kept for actions and progress (add, check out, the delivery steps), which keeps every screen calm and makes the next step obvious.
motion: A purple line draws the dragon in 14 strokes over 1.3 s, head first and eyes last. The lavender body and faint belly then fade in under the lines, which stay at full strength, and the wordmark rises 8 pt. The screen holds until 2.5 s, then cross-fades into Home. If the menu is still loading, the line fades to a ghost and redraws until it arrives, ending on the same tinted mark. Reduce Motion shows the finished mark.

screens.label: Launch
screens.note: A purple line draws the dragon in 14 strokes over 1.3 s, head first and eyes last. The lavender body and faint belly then fade in under the lines, which stay at full strength, and the wordmark rises 8 pt. The screen holds until 2.5 s, then cross-fades into Home. If the menu is still loading, the line fades to a ghost and redraws until it arrives, ending on the same tinted mark. Reduce Motion shows the finished mark.

screens.label: 21+ and location
screens.note: Massachusetts requires the 21+ check before the menu. Location comes next, and only roughly: it picks which store's menu you see. The street address is typed on the next screen.

screens.label: Delivery address
screens.note: The delivery address is always typed, with suggestions as you go. Location never fills it in, so the driver goes where you said.

screens.label: Home
screens.note: Photos do the selling. Store status and delivery time sit together at the top, so you know before browsing that delivery takes 40–50 minutes.

screens.label: Menu
screens.note: Four categories, as in the store: Flower, Pre-rolls, Vapes and Edibles. Every card has a real photo, price, brand and THC.

screens.label: Category and filters
screens.note: Filters are plain chips under the title, one tap each. The count tells you how much is left to scroll.

screens.label: Search
screens.note: Search matches names, brands and categories as you type. If nothing fits, the categories are right below.

screens.label: Product
screens.note: THC, size and the lab test date come first, then the description. The 21+ warning is part of the page, not a pop-up.

screens.label: Added to bag
screens.note: Adding keeps you browsing. The card turns into a stepper and the bag bar shows the count and subtotal.

screens.label: Bag
screens.note: Cash or debit at the door and the ID check are stated before checkout, so nothing at the door is a surprise. The bag shows the items, the fee, the taxes and the total, nothing else.

screens.label: Phone sign-in
screens.note: Sign-in waits until checkout: browsing never needs an account. The phone number is the account.

screens.label: Code entry
screens.note: Six boxes, one digit each. The code from Messages is offered above the keypad, so one tap fills it and places the order.

screens.label: Order placed
screens.note: One clear success moment: the arrival window, the order number and what to have ready at the door.

screens.label: Tracking: preparing
screens.note: Before a driver heads out, the map shows only your home. The four steps say where the order is.

screens.label: Tracking: on the way
screens.note: The map shows the driver's dragon badge and your home pin, nothing else: no route and no other stops. "2 stops before you" sets expectations without showing where.

screens.label: Tracking: arriving
screens.note: When you're the next stop, the sheet leads with what you need at the door: payment and ID.

screens.label: Tracking: delivered
screens.note: Delivered, with the time and the way to the receipt. The driver's position is no longer shown.

screens.label: Receipt
screens.note: Every line, the fee and the taxes, and how it was paid. Questions go to the store's phone line.

screens.label: Orders
screens.note: Past orders with their photos, so you recognize them at a glance, and a one-tap reorder.

screens.label: Account
screens.note: One list: address, location, text updates and the store's phone number. Deleting the account is in the app, not behind an email.

screens.label: Location turned off
screens.note: If you skipped location, Account offers to turn it on, with the one reason it's needed.

screens.label: Empty bag
screens.note: An empty bag points back to the menu and shows what's popular, with real photos.

screens.label: Store closed
screens.note: When the store is closed, Home says when it opens. You can still browse; the add buttons return at 1 PM.

screens.label: Order problem
screens.note: When something needs a person, the app says so plainly and puts the store's number in the main button. The store sorts it out with the driver.
